studies.one_line_summary: Field trials with wooden shading panels and reflective sheets showed taro LER above 1, with reflective sheets estimated to raise bifacial output about 20% and lower soil temperature.
studies.evidence_quote: Box–Cox-transformed random-intercept linear mixed-effects models showed significant associations of quantitative GCR, reflective-sheet treatment, and experimental year with taro yield

limitations_stated: hail protection based on a single event
energy output and LER are theoretical, model-based
future_work_stated: multi-season and multi-site studies
confirm hail protection benefit
confirm thermal regulation under a wider range of site conditions
studies.one_line_summary: Replicated off-grid agrivoltaic field trial in Atlixco found no lettuce or radish biomass loss, hail protection for cilantro, and higher model-based PV output from cooler temperatures.
studies.evidence_quote: environmental variables such as solar radiation and ambient temperature were monitored to calculate the theoretical efficiency and energy output of the PV panels

future_work_stated: further research on the proposed beam-splitter collector concept
studies.one_line_summary: Modelled spectral beam-splitter PV modules in an elevated agrivoltaic farm in Yuma, Arizona; season TDLI fell only 7% versus 43% for opaque PV.
studies.evidence_quote: This research evaluates the performance of spectral beam splitter integrated photovoltaic (BSIPV) modules using a PV performance model.

studies.one_line_summary: Ray-tracing simulations and a 5.5-month measurement campaign assessed white ground cloths; vertical bifacial showed no measurable gain while the tracker gained 25% rear irradiance.
studies.evidence_quote: a series of ray-tracing simulations and an extensive measurement campaign were conducted.

future_work_stated: evaluate the agrivoltaic system and the impact of increasing shade on the crop
assess trade-off between electricity production and crop production
studies.one_line_summary: Custom 1.5 m PARbar line sensors measured light interception by raspberry under solar panels; the crop received half the light but biomass fell less through compensation.
studies.evidence_quote: custom made PARbars were used: bars of 1.5 m long having light sensors every 5 cm facing the sky

studies.validation_metrics: NR (qualitative coherence with measured leaf temperatures)
studies.one_line_summary: An energy-balance sub-model of a crop model reproduced measured grapevine canopy temperature heterogeneity under dynamic agrivoltaics and illustrated model-based panel steering against heat stress.
studies.evidence_quote: the relevance of a mechanistic model to steer solar panels and protect plants from heat is illustrated through several examples.

studies.validation_metrics: agreement of simulated PARbar data with full modelled irradiance on plant rows
future_work_stated: compare irradiance distribution with observed plant adaptations to shading
studies.one_line_summary: BIGEYE ray-tracing modelled irradiance on soft-fruit rows under partially transparent PV, showing uneven irradiance between panel ends and between upper and lower canopy.
studies.evidence_quote: We modelled an agri-PV system of partially transparent PV panels integrated with a soft fruit farm using the light and PV simulation package BIGEYE.

studies.one_line_summary: Simulated vertical bifacial agrivoltaic arrays on New Jersey farms; double-high modules with bypass diodes and separate inverter strings nearly doubled power output per acre.
studies.evidence_quote: We present a model and study investigating the potential power output of vertical bifacial solar panels on New Jersey farms.

future_work_stated: optimise tracker strategy for local conditions (more light in cool humid, shading in hot dry conditions)
use actual crop models instead of soil irradiance
studies.one_line_summary: Simulated tracker-angle algorithms for an agri-PV strip-farming system; soil irradiance stayed at least 60% of open strip farming while electricity reached 20-66% of optimised HSAT.
studies.evidence_quote: we are developing algorithms for the solar trackers that will balance both crop demands and solar electricity yield.

studies.one_line_summary: Soil moisture observations at Pillnitz and Weesow were used to estimate evapotranspiration in dry periods, finding 44% higher rates under panels at Pillnitz but reversed patterns at Weesow.
studies.evidence_quote: the authors proceeded using soil moisture observations to quantify evapotranspiration pattern in dry periods.

studies.one_line_summary: Simulated light availability under elevated agrivoltaics with bifacial modules partly replaced by semi-transparent ones, examining module transparency and cell layout to suit crop needs.
studies.evidence_quote: a simulation model was conducted, which examined the impact of module transparency and cell layout based on light availability.

studies.one_line_summary: Simulated power generation and inter-panel shading of foldable, sun-adjusting panels in agrivoltaics, finding lower shading losses than fixed panels and strong seasonal variability.
studies.evidence_quote: Employing simulation techniques, the study investigates the impact of inter-panel shadow effects on power generation in systems using multiple foldable solar panels.

studies.crop_or_livestock: crop-type independent (farm loads: irrigation pumps, centre pivots, cow shed pumps)
studies.one_line_summary: Proposed size and dispatch co-optimisation for a grid-connected agrivoltaic system with stationary and vehicle batteries, improving economic feasibility for a conceptual New Zealand farm.
studies.evidence_quote: this paper introduces a novel agrivoltaic system energy planning optimisation method with an integrated dispatch scheduling framework.

studies.validation_metrics: R2 > 0.85 for front/rear irradiance and power output
studies.one_line_summary: Validated the AgriOptiCE bifacial PV model at Golden and Västerås (R2 > 0.85), finding hourly measured albedo gives the most accurate irradiance and power estimates.
studies.evidence_quote: AgriOptiCE is firstly validated by comparing estimated front and rear irradiances with on-site measurements for specific periods

studies.ai_methods_detail: unspecified clustering technique grouping simulated insolation profiles (19 clusters) as inputs to a point-based agricultural systems model
studies.one_line_summary: Clustered simulated daily insolation profiles for 81 layouts near Hobart into 19 groups feeding a crop model; optimal layout raised land productivity 47% retaining 80% pasture production.
studies.evidence_quote: A clustering technique was then applied to all insolation profiles to group them into rationally bounded cluster groups.

studies.crop_or_livestock: winter wheat, rapeseed and other arable crops
studies.validation_metrics: qualitative comparison of irradiance reduction trends and magnitudes with bifacial_radiance ray tracing
limitations_stated: in-depth validation of the entire framework not yet performed
future_work_stated: validate the entire framework when data from planned systems become available
develop advanced APV-related data products
studies.one_line_summary: Coupled a new APV shading model with the PROMET crop model to predict yields at a planned French tracker site; only 1P trackers kept wheat and rapeseed yields acceptable.
studies.evidence_quote: we developed a framework for simulating impacts of APV shading effects on crop yields.
studies.site_name: planned BayWa r.e. agrivoltaic project, France (location not specified)

studies.one_line_summary: Reported microclimate modelling and installation of a 48 kWp agrivoltaic system in Trondheim, Norway, the highest-latitude system, with initial Timothy grass biomass results.
studies.evidence_quote: we report on the modelling and installation of a 48 kWp agrivoltaic system at the Skjetlein High School in Trondheim (Norway, lat. 63.34)
